paper.title: The Blown Lead Paradox: A Pathwise Calibration Benchmark for Win Probability Forecasts
paper.title_of_first_version: The Blown Lead Paradox: Conditional Laws for the Running Maximum of Binary Doob Martingales

numbers_quoted_from_paper.note: ESPN public NFL feed, regular seasons 2018 to 2024, 1,848 games. These are the paper's numbers, not ours, and use a different model and sample.

notes.p0: the losing team's first win probability of the game (before the kickoff)
notes.peak: the losing team's largest win probability over all plays
notes.continuous_reference: P(peak >= x | lost) = p0 (1 - x) / (x (1 - p0)); expected counts are sums of this over games; intervals assume independent games
notes.first_crossing: expected blown leads = sum of (1 - p) at each team's first value at or above the threshold; exact for a calibrated model even when paths jump
notes.discrete_adjusted_reference: simulated calibrated game reported at play times, with time gaps fitted to the real jump sizes; an approximation, see docs/notes/m3b_blown_leads.md
notes.pit_bootstrap: season-stratified team (pigeonhole) bootstrap of the one-sided statistic d_upper, as in the paper
notes.wp_ours: out-of-fold predictions from scripts/fit_wp.py when present

discreteness_simulation.description: Simulated even game (p0 = 0.5): Brownian lead reported at n_steps play times. ratio = P(reported peak >= x | lost) / continuous formula. gap_shape null means equally spaced plays; a number means Gamma-distributed gaps.
